related_questions.question: How soon will a COVID test show positive?

text_blocks.snippet: A COVID-19 test, whether PCR or antigen, may show positive results as early as 2-3 days after infection, but it can also take longer, particularly with antigen tests. Antigen tests are less sensitive and may require repeat testing after a negative result to rule out infection. PCR tests, which are more sensitive, can detect the virus earlier but may still take up to 3 days to return results.
snippet_highlighted_words: as early as 2-3 days after infection

list.title: PCR tests:
list.snippet: These are highly sensitive and can detect even small amounts of the virus. They may show positive results as early as 2-3 days after infection, or even sooner in some cases. However, results can take up to 3 days to come back.

list.title: Antigen tests:
list.snippet: These are less sensitive and may not detect the virus as early as PCR tests. They are more likely to produce a false negative result, especially in the early stages of infection or in individuals with low viral loads. If you test negative with an antigen test but suspect you might have COVID-19, it's recommended to retest, according to the FDA.

list.title: Testing when symptomatic:
list.snippet: If you have symptoms of COVID-19, test immediately. If the initial test is negative, retest per the instructions, according to the FDA.

list.title: Testing after exposure:
list.snippet: If you've been exposed to someone with COVID-19 but don't have symptoms, wait at least 5 full days after the exposure before testing.
